hook: The AI stack for building a site solo

slides.headline: The AI stack for building a *site* solo
slides.body: Five tools, one job each, and the order to use them in. Save this before your next build.

slides.headline: Five tools. One *job* each.
slides.body: Most solo builders use too many tools at once. Give each one a single job and the stack gets quiet.

items.title: Claude Code
items.text: Anthropic's coding agent. Reads your repo, edits files and runs commands from your terminal.

items.title: Cursor
items.text: An AI code editor built on VS Code. Best when you want to see and steer every edit.

items.title: v0
items.text: Turns a prompt into UI as React and Tailwind code you can export and keep.

items.title: Figma
items.text: Where layout and spacing get decided before anyone prompts anything.

items.title: Vercel
items.text: Hosts the finished site and gives every change its own preview link.

slides.mascot_say: Five tabs open. Plan is working.

slides.headline: Write the *brief* before any tool opens
slides.body: Every tool above gives better output when it gets a better brief. Spend ten minutes here.

items.title: Audience
items.text: One sentence: the visitor, and what they already tried.

items.title: One action
items.text: Book a call, join the list, or buy. Pick one.

items.title: Sections
items.text: List them top to bottom. Order is a decision, so you make it.

items.title: Real copy
items.text: Paste the actual headline and price. Placeholder text gives placeholder pages.

slides.headline: Get the first *draft* on screen
slides.body: Use the agent for structure and the editor for fine-tuning. Don't polish yet.

items.title: Let the agent build
items.text: Give Claude Code the brief and one instruction: build only what the brief lists.

items.title: Keep prompts small
items.text: One section per prompt. Review each result before asking for the next.

items.title: Save your rules
items.text: Put fonts, colours and spacing in a DESIGN.md the agent reads every session.

items.title: Commit often
items.text: A commit after every working section gives you a safe place to go back to.

items.title: v0
cells: First pass at a section's UI

items.title: Figma
cells: Hand the spec to the agent

items.title: Vercel
cells: Check each preview on a phone

slides.headline: Prompting vs *briefing*
slides.body: The difference between a generic page and a usable one is mostly what you wrote before you started.
items: Make me a landing page | Brief with audience, sections, copy and one action
Looks modern | Two fonts, one accent, a spacing scale in DESIGN.md
Fix everything | One section per prompt, reviewed before the next
Done when it looks good | Done when it works at 375px wide

slides.headline: Before you *ship* it
slides.body: Run these on the live preview link, not on your local copy.

items.title: Every button goes somewhere
items.text: Click each one, twice.

items.title: Checked at 375px wide
items.text: Scroll every section on a phone-sized screen.

items.title: Contact form reaches you
items.text: Submit it and find the entry where it should land.

items.title: Share image works
items.text: Paste the link into a DM to yourself and look.

items.title: One honest person has seen it
items.text: Ask what they think the page wants them to do.

slides.headline: Habits that keep you at *$0*
slides.body: Seven habits, with the fix for each. Check how many you recognise.

slides.headline: Building before *asking*
slides.body: This is the habit that costs the most, because it feels like progress the whole time.

items.title: A dashboard nobody requested
items.text: Features feel productive. Requests are what tell you which feature matters.

items.title: Zero conversations with a buyer
items.text: You can't know what they'd pay for if you've never asked.

items.title: The launch post comes first
items.text: Posting before any conversation gets you applause, not customers.

slides.headline: Rebuilding the stack every *Monday*
slides.body: A new tool is a way to avoid the hard part while still feeling busy.

items.title: The symptom
items.text: New framework, new UI kit, same empty inbox.

items.title: The cause
items.text: The tool was never the bottleneck. Talking to buyers is.

items.title: The fix
items.text: Pick a stack for 90 days. Write the date on it.

items.title: The rule
items.text: A new tool needs a customer problem it solves, not a launch post.

slides.headline: Polishing the logo, not the *offer*
slides.body: Nobody buys a gradient. They buy a clear answer to what they get and what it costs.

items.title: The symptom
items.text: Five logo versions, zero price on the page.

items.title: The fix
items.text: Write the offer in one sentence a stranger can repeat.

items.title: The test
items.text: Ask someone to explain it back to you. If they can't, rewrite it.

items.title: The order
items.text: Offer, then page, then brand. In that order.

slides.headline: Pricing by *vibes*
slides.body: Picking the safe number is the same as picking no number.

items.title: The symptom
items.text: You choose a price because it feels comfortable, not because anyone said it.

items.title: The fix
items.text: Ask three people what they'd pay for the outcome, not the file.

items.title: The check
items.text: If nobody flinches, you're probably too low.

items.title: The rule
items.text: Change the price before you change the product.

slides.headline: How it feels vs what it *is*
slides.body: Every one of these sounds reasonable when you say it. That is how they survive.
items: "Almost ready" | Not shipped
"Building in public" | Posting screenshots
"Waiting for the right moment" | Avoiding the DMs
"Doing research" | Another week of tools
"I need one more feature" | You need one more conversation
slides.stat: HOW IT FEELS | WHAT IT IS

slides.headline: One habit to drop *this week*
slides.body: Pick one. Not all seven.

items.title: Monday
items.text: Delete the tool tabs you opened this month and haven't used.

items.title: Tuesday
items.text: Write the offer in one sentence and read it out loud.

items.title: Wednesday
items.text: Send the same short message to five people who have the problem.

items.title: Thursday
items.text: Write down the one thing someone said that surprised you.

items.title: Friday
items.text: Build only what that sentence asked for.

hook: Build a launch page in six sections

slides.headline: Build a launch page in *six* sections
slides.body: What goes in each one, and the prompt to give your AI agent.

slides.headline: *Hero*: who it's for
slides.body: The first screen decides whether anyone scrolls. It has one job.

items.title: Headline
items.text: Who it's for and what they get, in under ten words.

items.title: Subline
items.text: One sentence on how, in plain words.

items.title: One button
items.text: The single action. Not two. Not a menu of options.

items.title: Prompt
items.text: "Write three headlines for [who] who want [outcome]. Plain words, no hype."

slides.headline: *Proof*: show it's real
slides.body: Only real work and facts you can verify. Invented proof gets found out.

items.title: Have results?
items.text: Show them with the context: what, for whom, how long.

items.title: No results yet?
items.text: Show your process or a sample you made for this page.

items.title: Never
items.text: Fake logos, made-up reviews, numbers you can't back up.

items.title: Prompt
items.text: "Turn these facts into three proof points. Don't add numbers I didn't give you."

slides.headline: *How it works* in three steps
slides.body: A stranger should understand the offer in ten seconds.

items.title: Step one
items.text: What they do first, in one sentence.

items.title: Step two
items.text: What you do, in one sentence.

items.title: Step three
items.text: What they get, in one sentence.

items.title: Prompt
items.text: "Explain how [offer] works in three steps. One sentence each, no jargon."

slides.headline: The *offer*: be specific
slides.body: Vague offers get ignored. Specific ones get questions.

items.title: What's included
items.text: A list of exactly what they receive.

items.title: The price
items.text: Show it. Hidden prices cost you the buyers who'd have paid.

items.title: What happens next
items.text: The first thing that happens after they say yes.

items.title: Prompt
items.text: "Write the offer block from this and nothing else: included, price, timeline."

slides.headline: *FAQ*: answer the doubt
slides.body: Write the questions a hesitant buyer asks, not the ones you wish they'd ask.

items.title: How much, exactly?
items.text: State the price and what changes it.

items.title: How long does it take?
items.text: Give the real timeline, including their part.

items.title: Is this for me?
items.text: Say who it's for and who it isn't.

items.title: What if I'm not happy?
items.text: Say what you'll do. Only promise what you'll honour.

slides.headline: Launch page vs *homepage*
slides.body: One is a decision. The other is a directory. Know which one you are building.
items: Ten links | One action
Written for everyone | Written for one visitor
Redesigned forever | Done when it converts
Explains the whole company | Makes one argument

hook: 15 checks before you ship an AI-built site

slides.headline: 15 checks before you ship the site *Claude* built
slides.body: Run these before you post the link, not after someone DMs you a screenshot.

items.title: No lorem ipsum left
items.text: Search the page for "lorem" and "placeholder".

items.title: Every button goes somewhere
items.text: Click each one. Twice.

items.title: Prices match the checkout
items.text: Compare the page, the checkout and any emails.

items.title: The contact email receives
items.text: Send a test from a different address.

items.title: Checked at 375px wide
items.text: Dev tools, a phone size, scroll every section.

items.title: Tap targets fit a thumb
items.text: Buttons and links you can hit without zooming.

items.title: No sideways scroll
items.text: If the page wobbles, something is too wide.

items.title: Text readable without zooming
items.text: Body text, buttons and form labels.

items.title: Page title and description set
items.text: This is what shows in search and when shared.

items.title: Share image works in a DM
items.text: Paste the link to yourself and look.

items.title: Forms tested end to end
items.text: Submit it, then find the entry where it should land.

items.title: Analytics counts once
items.text: One visit should be one visit, not two.

slides.headline: The *human* bit
slides.body: Three checks no tool will do for you.

items.title: Open it on someone else's phone
items.text: Their screen, their browser, their signal.

items.title: Send it to one honest person
items.text: Ask what they thought the page wanted them to do.

items.title: Read the headline out loud
items.text: If you stumble, rewrite it.

slides.headline: What AI checks vs what you *check*
slides.body: The agent says it works. You find out whether it works for a person.
items: Code that runs | A page a stranger understands
Layout that renders | Layout that works on a phone
A form that submits | A form that reaches your inbox
Analytics installed | Analytics counting once

slides.headline: Fifteen checks. About *ten* minutes.
slides.body: Most of them take under a minute. The ones that don't are the ones that would have hurt.

items.title: Do them in order
items.text: Content, mobile, technical, then the human bit.

items.title: Do them on the live link
items.text: Your local copy hides half the problems.
